solves: Takes the person from one page to another in a long list and shows where in the list they are.
use_when: With type numbered, below a common list or search result, when the person jumps between nearby pages.
With type simple or compact, in a narrow space: compact fits a card header, a side panel and a phone.
With type edges, with go to page, in a long list, when the person needs to reach the start, the end or a given page.
With type range, when the total of items matters more than the page number.
With type table, in the footer of a data table with many records.
do_not_use_when: To filter or search the list: pagination splits the result, it does not replace the filter or the search.
To load more or scroll without end: they are not part of this piece.
To move between the steps of a flow: pagination moves between pages of the same list.

type.constraint: The Figma tipo. numbered: numbers with Previous and Next written. simple: arrows and the position text. edges: numbers with first, previous, next and last. range: arrows and the range of items. compact: arrows and the short position text. table: items per page, the range and the bar with first and last. Outside the list, the piece draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

page.constraint: The current page, a whole number from 1. The piece changes it when the person moves. Above the count, the last page is drawn and one warning is emitted in development: a filter that shrinks the list does not take the bar away.

page-count.constraint: The number of pages, a whole number from 0. Required unless total-items and page-size give the count; with both, the derived count is drawn and one warning is emitted when they differ. A count of zero draws nothing, with no error.

total-items.constraint: The total of items of the list, a whole number from 0. Required in range and table, which show the range of items.

page-size.constraint: The items per page, a whole number from 1. Required in range and table. In table, the person changes it through items per page, and the first item on screen stays on screen.

page-sizes.constraint: The options of items per page, whole numbers from 1, and only in table, where it is required and holds page-size. As an attribute, a JSON list.

go-to-page.constraint: Turns on go to page: an nph-input in pagination/page-input-width beside the bar. Only in edges, the bar with first and last; it needs go-to-label.

label.constraint: The name of the navigation, already localized, such as Pagination. Without it, the piece renders and warns once in development.

page-label.constraint: The name of each number, with the {page} marker, such as Page {page}. Without it, the number is named by the number itself and the piece warns once in development.

first-label.constraint: The name and the balloon text of the first arrow. Required in edges and table.

previous-label.constraint: The name and the balloon text of the previous arrow. In numbered, the written text of the button, with no balloon.

next-label.constraint: The name and the balloon text of the next arrow. In numbered, the written text of the button, with no balloon.

last-label.constraint: The name and the balloon text of the last arrow. Required in edges and table.

position-text.constraint: The position text, already localized, with the {page}, {count}, {start}, {end} and {total} markers, filled with the numbers in the language of the page. Required in simple, compact, range and table.

page-size-label.constraint: The visible label of items per page, which is also the name of its nph-select. Required in table.

go-to-label.constraint: The visible label of go to page, which is also the name of its nph-input. Required with go-to-page.

nph-page-change.constraint: Fired on the host (bubbles, composed) only when the person moves: a number, an arrow, go to page or items per page, with detail { page, pageSize }. Setting page from code fires nothing. The input and change of the inner fields do not leave the piece.

numbered.choose_when: A common list or search result, when the person jumps between nearby pages.

simple.choose_when: A narrow space where the word page fits.

edges.choose_when: A long list, when the person needs the start, the end or a given page; the only type with go to page.

range.choose_when: When the total of items matters more than the page number.

compact.choose_when: A card header, a side panel or a phone.

table.choose_when: The footer of a data table with many records.

page-rest.changes_for_user: A number with no background, in text/label-md (D-2).

page-hover.changes_for_user: The number gains the hover background.

page-current.changes_for_user: The current page: background and the number in text/label-md-strong, with aria-current=page.

arrow-rest.changes_for_user: The arrow on pagination/arrow-background with a pagination/arrow-border stroke inside; the icon light.

arrow-hover.changes_for_user: The arrow gains the hover background and the icon goes solid; the balloon opens after the wait.

arrow-disabled.changes_for_user: The arrow without a destination stays in place at pagination/disabled-opacity, out of the Tab order, with no hover and no balloon.

focus.changes_for_user: Keyboard focus on a number or an arrow: border border/width in focus/border and halo focus/ring-width in focus/halo, outside the button; on an arrow, the balloon opens at once.

business_rules: The first and the last page are always shown; above seven pages, the numbers keep seven slots, with an ellipsis for each run of hidden pages.
The arrow without a destination is disabled, never hidden: the bar keeps its width.
Reaching the first or last page by an arrow moves the focus to the current page, or to the opposite arrow where there are no numbers.
Changing the items per page keeps the first item on screen.
Go to page takes a whole number; past the end it goes to the last page, and text that is not a number is ignored. The field empties after it.

tokens.bar: border pagination/border-width in pagination/border, radius pagination/radius, padding pagination/padding-x and pagination/padding-y, gap pagination/item-gap
tokens.groups: pagination/group-gap between groups, pagination/control-gap between a label and its field
tokens.page: pagination/item-size square, radius pagination/item-radius, text pagination/text-foreground in text/label-md (D-2)
tokens.arrow: pagination/item-size square, radius pagination/item-radius, background pagination/arrow-background, stroke pagination/arrow-border-width in pagination/arrow-border, icon/size-md; hover pagination/item-background-hover
tokens.written-arrow: in numbered, space/control-padding on the sides and space/inline-tight between icon and text, as the nph-button with text
tokens.focus: border border/width in focus/border, focus/border-radius-control; halo focus/ring-width in focus/halo, focus/radius-control-with-border

ai_hints: Use nph-pagination below a list or table that does not fit on one screen; to filter or search, use the filter or the search.
Choose compact in a card header, a side panel or a phone, instead of shrinking the buttons.
Choose table in the footer of a data table, with page-size equal to the rows the table shows.
Choose range when the total of items matters more than the page number.
Give every text already localized: label, page-label and the arrow labels are the names the screen reader reads.
Listen to nph-page-change to load the page; do not listen to click.

accessibility.semantics: A navigation landmark (nav) named by label. Each number and each arrow is a native button; the current page carries aria-current=page. The ellipsis is hidden from the screen reader.
accessibility.accessible_name: Each number is named by page-label; the icon-only arrows are named by their balloon text (first-label, previous-label, next-label, last-label), through aria-labelledby, announced once; in numbered, the written text names the arrow. Items per page and go to page are named by their visible labels.
keyboard: Tab: walks the arrows, the numbers and the fields in reading order; a disabled arrow is skipped.
Enter or Space: moves to the page of the number or the arrow.
In go to page, Enter goes to the typed page.
accessibility.focus: Border focus/border and halo focus/halo outside the number or the arrow, keyboard only; the balloon of an arrow opens with it.
accessibility.contrast: The number, the text and the icon in pagination/text-foreground pass 4.5:1 in both modes, also over pagination/item-background-active and pagination/item-background-hover; the arrow border in pagination/arrow-border passes 3:1; the focus border passes 3:1 against the halo and the current page background.
accessibility.color_alternative: The current page also has the number in bold (text/label-md-strong) and aria-current; the disabled arrow also leaves the Tab order.

invalid_combinations: A type outside the six — the piece draws nothing.
A page, page-count, total-items or page-size that is not a whole number in range — the count cannot be drawn.
No page count: no page-count, and no total-items with page-size.
range or table without total-items and page-size — the range of items cannot be written.
table without page-sizes, with page-sizes that do not hold page-size, or without page-size-label; page-sizes outside table.
go-to-page outside edges, or without go-to-label.
No previous-label or next-label; edges or table without first-label or last-label — the arrows would have no name.
simple, compact, range or table without position-text.
anti_patterns: Hiding the arrow without a destination: the bar jumps. Use the disabled arrow.
Marking the current page only by the color of the number: color alone is not a signal.
Using a different items per page from the table: the range would not match the rows on screen.
Shrinking the buttons on a narrow screen instead of using compact.
Using pagination to filter, to search, to load more or to scroll without end.
